what: Barclays is a British bank with two halves: a UK retail and business bank, and a global investment bank strong in fixed income trading and debt underwriting. It is also one of the largest credit card issuers in the United States.
customers: UK households and businesses, global corporations and institutional investors, and US credit card holders through retail partnerships.
money: trading, debt and equity underwriting and advisory
UK current accounts, mortgages and cards
co-branded credit cards with US retailers
moat: One of only a few non-American banks with real scale in global fixed income trading, alongside a protected UK retail deposit base.
risks: Trading revenue is volatile and consumes capital
UK regulators ring-fence the retail bank, limiting how capital moves
US card losses rise when American consumers come under pressure
Past conduct issues have brought repeated fines
opportunities: A multi-year plan to return capital through buybacks is well under way
Analysts see about 30% upside to the current price
watch: Return on tangible equity and investment bank revenue against US rivals.
